samples.summary: New `abortImageResizeDrag()` calls in undoFn / redoFn / resetAfterDocumentReplace have no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds `abortImageResizeDrag()` to `undoFn`, `redoFn` and `resetAfterDocumentReplace`, with the stated failure mode: "left armed, its `mouseup` would commit a size onto whatever the undo put at that coordinate" / "the next `mouseup` anywhere would run the commit path against the replaced document" — i.e. a silent document mutation with the wrong size on the wrong inline. copy-integrity.test.ts covers only the sibling `selectedImage = null` in those three functions ('a toolbar undo clears it', 'a toolbar redo clears it', 'resetAfterDocumentReplace clears it'); none of them arms a drag first, and none dispatches a later mousemove/mouseup. Nothing else touches the drag: grep for `imageResize`/`se handle` across packages/docs/test matches only editor-read-only.test.ts (which drives the read-only/editable gate) and text-box-editor.test.ts. The new `dragSouthEast`/`pressSouthEast` helpers in editor-read-only.test.ts prove the gesture is drivable in jsdom, so this is testable: press the handle, call `editor.undo()`, then mousemove+mouseup and assert the size did not change. Deleting all three `abortImageResizeDrag()` calls leaves the suite green.

samples.summary: Three new `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` call sites are untested: mergeTableCells, applySpellSuggestion, insertPageNumber
samples.evidence: copy-integrity.test.ts loops a `tableOps` list covering deleteTable, insertTableRow, deleteTableRow, insertTableColumn, deleteTableColumn and splitTableCell — `mergeTableCells` is absent from the list. `applySpellSuggestion` and `insertPageNumber` also received new clear calls in this diff and appear nowhere in packages/docs/test (grep for `applySpellSuggestion|insertPageNumber|mergeTableCells` under packages/docs/test returns no matches). Removing the clear at any of those three sites leaves the suite green, while the diff's own reasoning is that a surviving stale selection makes Delete remove the wrong image.

samples.summary: The find-bar's new `editor?.clearImageSelection()` calls before replaceActive/replaceAll are untested — no find-bar test file exists
samples.evidence: docs-find-bar.tsx gains `editor?.clearImageSelection()` in `handleReplace` and `handleReplaceAll`. Glob for `packages/frontend/tests/**/*find*` returns no files, and grep for `clearImageSelection` across packages matches only the source, docs-find-bar.tsx and packages/docs tests. The docs-side test 'the exported clearImageSelection drops it, for out-of-module mutators' exercises the editor API directly and its own comment names the find bar as the consumer, but nothing pins that the find bar actually calls it — the wiring can be dropped undetected.

samples.summary: `textEditorRef?.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse(e)` on the image mousedown path has no test — read-only link-following on hyperlinked images is unpinned
samples.evidence: The diff adds a new public `TextEditor.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` solely so a viewer's click on a *hyperlinked image* still opens the link now that `handleImageMouseDown` claims the event with `stopImmediatePropagation()` in read-only. grep for `recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` finds only the two source sites (text-editor.ts:1637, editor.ts:2665) and no test. editor-read-only.test.ts mentions link paths only in its header comment ('pointer/copy/link paths that need real pixel layout are covered by manual / browser tests'), yet the new read-only describe in that same file now does drive real pixel geometry, so an image-with-link click test is feasible. Removing the call silently takes link-following on images away from viewers.

samples.summary: DocCanvas's readOnly → `{ handles: !this.readOnly }` wiring is untested; only the overlay primitive's new option is covered
samples.evidence: image-selection-overlay.test.ts adds 'draws the border alone when handles are off', which calls `drawImageSelection(ctx, rect, { handles: false })` directly — it pins the primitive, not that DocCanvas passes `readOnly` through, nor that `new DocCanvas(canvas, readOnly)` in editor.ts:951 forwards the flag. grep for `new DocCanvas` shows only the production site; no test constructs a DocCanvas. If the wiring regressed, a viewer would see eight resize handles that do nothing — exactly the outcome the diff's comments call out.

samples.summary: The new `if (readOnly) return false;` in handleImageHover is not exercised by any hover (mousemove) test
samples.evidence: The read-only tests assert `resizeCursorCount(container)).toBe(0)` only after a *mousedown* (`pressSouthEast`) or a plain selecting click; the hover override lives in `handleImageHover`, which runs on mousemove over a handle without any drag in flight. No test dispatches a bare mousemove over a handle in read-only, so removing the new guard (viewer sees a nwse-resize cursor over a handle that is neither painted nor actionable) leaves the suite green.
searchedFor: read the new 'read-only image resize drag' describe in editor-read-only.test.ts
grep mousemove in copy-integrity.test.ts and editor-read-only.test.ts

samples.summary: The `getBlock` → `findBlock` hardening in handleImageResizeMouseUp (block deleted mid-drag) has no test
samples.evidence: copy-integrity.test.ts pins the equivalent hardening for the copy provider ('writes nothing when a peer deleted the block under the selection') and for delete ('Delete deletes nothing when a peer deleted the block') using the store.setDocument + `getDoc().refresh()` pattern, but no test applies that pattern to an in-flight resize drag. The stated failure is an exception escaping a document-level `mouseup` listener. The drag helpers now available in editor-read-only.test.ts make this reachable.

samples.summary: The `render()` newly added to imageKeyHandler's catch-all is not pinned by the test that covers that branch
samples.evidence: The diff adds `render()` next to `selectedImage = null` in the catch-all so a key TextEditor ignores (F5, dead key) does not leave a stale selection overlay painted. The corresponding test, 'a non-modifier key still drops the image selection', asserts only `expect(editor.getSelectedImage()).toBeNull()` after pressing F5 — true with or without the render call. The stale-overlay behavior the change exists for is therefore untested.
searchedFor: read copy-integrity.test.ts 'a non-modifier key still drops the image selection'

samples.summary: 'the copy/cut shortcut is left uncancelled' assertions would pass even with the fix removed
samples.evidence: Both tests assert only `pressCopyShortcut(...).defaultPrevented === false`. If `imageKeyHandler` did not absorb Cmd/Ctrl+C at all, the event falls through to `TextEditor.handleKeyDown`, which (text-editor.ts:883-950) does not preventDefault a plain mod+c in either editable or read-only mode — so `defaultPrevented` stays false and the assertion passes while the image selection is being cleared (the #870 bug). The companion tests ('does not drop the image selection') carry the real signal; these two, whose comments claim to be the tests that catch a `preventDefault()` regression, are near-vacuous on their own.

samples.summary: New describe installs the canvas shim in beforeEach but its afterEach only restores the geometry shim
samples.evidence: The added 'read-only image resize drag' describe calls `installCanvasShim()` in `beforeEach`, while its `afterEach` calls only `restoreGeometryShim()` and clears the body — `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext` is left stubbed (the outer describe's afterEach, which restores it, does not apply to this sibling describe). Harmless under vitest's per-file isolation, but it leaves a global patched for anything appended to the file later.
searchedFor: read beforeEach/afterEach of the new describe in editor-read-only.test.ts

verdict.reason: The three `abortImageResizeDrag()` calls exist (editor.ts:2110 undoFn, :2146 redoFn, :3953 resetAfterDocumentReplace) and the helper (editor.ts:2587-2593) tears down document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners plus the canvas cursor, guarding the commit path at editor.ts:2522-2571 that writes a size onto the captured (blockId, offset). No test exercises that teardown. Repo-wide greps for `abortImageResizeDrag`, `selectImageAt`, `mouseup`/`mousemove` in test dirs, and cursor/removeEventListener assertions turn up only two editor-level suites: editor-read-only.test.ts:396-558, which drives the real se-handle gesture but never calls undo/redo/resetAfterDocumentReplace, and copy-integrity.test.ts:1084-1175, whose three tests only call selectImageAt then undo()/redo()/resetAfterDocumentReplace() and assert getSelectedImage() is null — no drag is armed and no later mousemove/mouseup is dispatched, so they pass identically with the abort calls removed. image-selection-overlay.test.ts is a pure-function suite (handleCenter/hitTestImageHandle/computeResizeDelta/computePreviewRect) that never constructs an editor, and packages/docs/src has no colocated tests. The gap is real and, since the untested failure silently commits a wrong size onto a wrong inline in the document, it is major under the missing-tests rubric.
